title: Suspense Resource Promise Wrapper (wrapPromise)
concept: Suspense Protocol: Throwing Promises on Pending State
problemStatement: Implement `wrapPromise(promise)` that returns an object with a `read()` method. If the promise is pending, `read()` MUST throw the promise itself. If rejected, it throws the error. If resolved, it returns the resolved data.
interviewTrap: Throwing a promise is how React Suspense detects async loading. If wrapPromise is instantiated inside the render body instead of cached, a new Promise is created on every render, locking the UI in an infinite suspension loop.

testCases.name: Throws the suspender promise while pending
testCases.input: resource.read() on pending promise throws Promise
testCases.testFn: const p = new Promise(() => {}); const resource = wrapPromise(p); try { resource.read(); return false; } catch (thrown) { return thrown instanceof Promise; }

testCases.name: Returns data synchronously once resolved
testCases.testFn: const p = Promise.resolve('DataLoaded'); const resource = wrapPromise(p); return p.then(() => resource.read());

testCases.name: Throws error when rejected
testCases.testFn: const p = Promise.reject(new Error('NetworkFail')); const resource = wrapPromise(p); return p.catch(() => {}).then(() => { try { resource.read(); return false; } catch (e) { return e.message; } });

detailedExplanation.conceptualOverview: When a component suspends, it throws a Promise up the Fiber tree. React catches the promise, pauses the render phase for that branch, renders the nearest Suspense fallback, and resumes when the promise resolves.

2. Reconciliation: Double buffering and fiber diffing mechanics.
3. Commit Phase: Synchronous/passive effect execution and DOM mutation.

interviewCrossQuestions.question: How does React Suspense work under the hood? What does a component throw?
interviewCrossQuestions.answer: React Suspense relies on **throwing Promises**! When a component attempts to read data that is not yet ready, the resource reader literally throws the pending Promise: `throw promise;`. React catches the thrown Promise inside its render work loop (via `throwException`), suspends rendering of that component subtree, mounts the nearest `<Suspense fallback={...}>` fallback to the screen, and attaches `.then()` to the promise. When the promise resolves, React restarts the render pass!
interviewCrossQuestions.whyAsked: The #1 core architectural question for React Suspense.

interviewCrossQuestions.question: What are the three states of a Suspense resource wrapper?
interviewCrossQuestions.answer: 1) `pending`: reading throws the Promise. 2) `success`: reading returns the resolved data. 3) `error`: reading throws the caught Error instance (caught by nearest Error Boundary).
interviewCrossQuestions.whyAsked: Tests understanding of the wrapPromise protocol.

howToExplain.opening: React Suspense works by catching thrown Promises during the render phase, pausing component rendering and displaying a fallback until the Promise resolves.
keyPoints: Components throw a Promise when data is pending.
React catches the Promise and mounts the Suspense fallback.
Attaches .then() to re-trigger rendering upon resolution.
Standardized in React 19 as the native use(promise) hook.
howToExplain.closingImpression: Suspense turns asynchronous data fetching into declarative synchronous-looking code.
analogies: A waiter at a restaurant: you ask for soup; the waiter says 'the soup is simmering, here is some bread (fallback) while you wait', and brings the soup when ready.

commonMistakes.mistake: Creating a new fetch promise inside the render body without caching.
commonMistakes.why: On every render retry, a fresh promise is instantiated, causing infinite suspense loops.
commonMistakes.correct: Cache promises outside render or use React.cache / SWR / TanStack Query.

followUpDeepDive.question: Where in React reconciler source is the thrown Promise caught?
followUpDeepDive.answer: In `packages/react-reconciler/src/ReactFiberWorkLoop.js` inside `throwException()`, which marks the fiber with `ShouldCapture` and finds the nearest `SuspenseComponent`.
